findings.title: A prolonged student disconnect is converted into a graded partial interview
findings.why_it_matters: The change deliberately prevents AgentSession from closing when the only participant leaves, but adds no participant-absence watchdog or paused state. If the student cannot rejoin, the agent stays alive until budget_watch sets finished; aborted remains false and the normal exit reports finished=true. That reaches agent-complete and completeInterview, so the LMS grades whatever partial transcript exists and consumes the attempt. This violates the recovery invariant precisely for the cut-off case the patch is meant to repair.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep close_on_disconnect disabled for a short rejoin grace period, but observe participant leave/join events. Cancel the grace timer on a valid rejoin; when it expires, set an explicit aborted/not-completable state and report recording only (finished=false), never the normal budget completion. Alternatively pause the interview clock while no student is present, with a bounded expiry that requires instructor-reviewed recovery. Add an integration test that drops the only participant past the grace period and proves no grading enqueue/status=completed occurs.
evidence: lms/agent/main.py:1036-1044 -- budget_watch sets finished when the fixed interview budget elapses, with no check that a participant is present.
lms/agent/main.py:1052-1061 -- aborted is set only when AgentSession emits close before finished; the new close_on_disconnect=False prevents the disconnect from taking this route.
lms/agent/main.py:1084 -- the normal budget exit calls stop_and_report_recording(finished=not aborted), which is true after a participant-less budget expiry.
lms/app/api/interview/agent-complete/route.ts:72-80 -- finished=true calls completeInterview, which marks the interview completed and enqueues grading.

residual_risks: Finalized conversation items are persisted through untracked asyncio.create_task calls (lms/agent/main.py:1023), while normal completion is posted after session.drain (lines 1072-1084). session.drain does not establish that those HTTP writes finished, so a slow final student or agent turn can be rejected after status becomes completed and omitted from grading.

The new global heartbeat check establishes artifact identity and HTTP reachability, not successful LiveKit worker registration or room-specific job attachment. A healthy-looking reporter can therefore still admit a room with no interviewer.
LiveKit Egress quota exhaustion remains best-effort. Live dialogue may complete and grade without the promised room recording until the account quota is restored.
testing_gaps: No test keeps close_on_disconnect=False, removes the sole participant, advances the interview clock, and verifies the partial interview stays live/ungraded after the rejoin grace period.
No test proves all asynchronous agent-turn posts settle before agent-complete changes interview status, including a deliberately delayed final turn.

No end-to-end canary exercises the full sequence: healthy worker admission, spoken simulated student turns, brief disconnect/rejoin with the same interview ID, normal completion, and exactly one worker grading job.
